and an opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been

Public Comments

   City Council Special Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, October 27, 2020

   CALL TO ORDER
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

 1. PUBLIC COMMENT

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PUBLIC WORKS STREET PAVING PROGRAM UPDATE

 3. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESPONSE TO THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY CIVIL GRAND JURY’S 2019-2020 REPORT

  Every year, the Los Angeles County Civil Grand Jury releases a report that
  reviews many city and county functions. This year’s report has two sections,
  landfills and public detention facilities that pertain to the City of San Gabriel.
  Both sections require a formal response from the City. The report describes
  the Civil Grand Jury Report sections and a recommended response from the
  City.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign, and
  direct staff to submit the attached response by October 30, 2020.

  B. CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR 2020 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) LOCAL STREETS SLURRY SEAL PROJECT,
  CONTRACT NO. 20-11

  All American Asphalt is the lowest responsive bidder for the construction
  contract of the 2020 CDBG Local Streets Slurry Seal Project with the amount
  of $218,040. This project will apply slurry treatment to 12 local street
  segments within qualifying CDBG areas. The project is primarily funded
  through the Los Angeles County Community Development Block Grant

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – October 27, 2020  2
   (CDBG) Funds. The 2020 CDBG Local Streets Slurry Seal Project is designated
  for the low and moderate-income residential areas. So far, there has been 12
  approved street segments for this Fiscal Year 2020-21 CDBG Street
  Improvement Project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve plans and specifications for the 2020 CDBG Local Streets Slurry
  Seal Project, Contract No. 20-11;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute contract documents with All
  American Asphalt for the total bid amount in the amount of $218,040; and
  3. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $239,844 which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

  C. CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR 2020 PAVEMENT REHABILITATION
  PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-12

  All American Asphalt is the lowest responsive bidder for the construction
  contract of the 2020 Pavement Rehabilitation Project with the amount of
  $1,195,276. This project will apply asphalt rubber aggregate membrane
  (ARAM) and slurry seal treatment for 9 lane miles of roadways.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive all minor bid irregularities as immaterial and award a contract to All
  American Asphalt for the 2020 Pavement Rehabilitation Project, Contract
  No. 20-12;
  2. Reject the submitted bid protest filed by Manhole Adjusting Incorporated
  as without merit;
  3. Approve plans and specifications for the 2020 Pavement Rehabilitation
  Project, Contract No. 20-12;
  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute contract documents with All
  American Asphalt for the total bid amount in the amount of $1,195,276;
  and
  5. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $1,314,804 which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

 City Council Special Meeting Agenda – October 27, 2020  3
   A. ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES OPTIONS

  At the City Council meetings of June 16 and June 20, 2020, City Council
  discussed the ongoing increase in service costs of the full-service animal care
  and control services contract, and directed staff to explore other alternatives
  while executing a 6-month Agreement with the San Gabriel Valley Humane
  Society, at a cost of $175,000 to include retaining animal licensing fees
  collected from residents, averaging $40,000 per year. Staff has implemented
  the contract while exploring alternatives for City Council’s consideration. The
  staff report provides (a) a summary of research, including legal requirements
  for providing animal control, (b) options and costs of assuming animal control
  responsibilities, and cost of animal control contracts in surrounding cities, and
  (c) a new proposal from the San Gabriel Valley Humane Society for the 2021-
  22 Fiscal Year with significant cost savings for full-service, sheltering and after-
  hours service, and sheltering contract options.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review the information provided, and
  direct staff to research additional information or return with a specific
  recommendation for City Council’s consideration.

  5. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 17,
  2020 at 6:30 p.m. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at
www.sangabrielcity.com/agendacenter. Materials related to an item on this Agenda, submitted
to the City Council after distribution of the Agenda packet, will be posted on the City website.

Persons with Disabilities. Upon request, this Agenda will be made available in appropriate

Persons requesting a Translator. Any person requesting translation for the meeting must

Questions about this Agenda? Should any person have a question concerning any of the above
Agenda items prior to the meeting, please contact the City Clerk at cityclerk@sgch.org during
regular office hours.

MINUTES OF OCTOBER 27, 2020
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:35 P.M. on Tuesday, October 27, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating
by teleconference.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Arminé
  Chaparyan, City Attorney Keith Lemieux, Police Chief
  Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public
  Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Debbie Kilgore provided comments requesting that the City allow garage sales to
  occur at this time.

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PUBLIC WORKS STREET PAVING PROGRAM UPDATE

  The staff presentation was made by Public Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck.

3. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Vice Mayor Liao pulled Item 4A for separate discussion.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4B – 4C as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4B – 4C as presented by a vote of 5-0 as
  follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  October 27, 2020
   ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Regarding Item 4A, Vice Mayor Liao commented on grants, funding, incentives, and
  education related to food-waste recycling, and thanked Athens Services for a recent
  compost give-away.

  City Manager Lazzaretto explained that the City’s recent contract amendment with
  Athens Services enables the City to meet the requirements of recent legislation and
  that Athens will partner on educational outreach in the community.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to approve
  Consent Calendar Item 4A as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Item 4A as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESPONSE TO THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY CIVIL GRAND JURY’S 2019-2020 REPORT

  The City Council authorized the Mayor to sign, and directed staff to submit the
  response by October 30, 2020.

  B. CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR 2020 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT (CDBG) LOCAL STREETS SLURRY SEAL PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-
  11

  The City Council:

  1. Approved the plans and specifications for the 2020 CDBG Local Streets Slurry
  Seal Project, Contract No. 20-11;
  2. Authorized the City Manager to execute contract documents with All American
  Asphalt for the total bid amount in the amount of $218,040; and
  3. Approved a Purchase Order in the amount of $239,844 which includes a 10%
  construction contingency.

  C. CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR  2020  PAVEMENT  REHABILITATION
  PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-12

  The City Council:

  1. Waived all minor bid irregularities as immaterial and awarded a contract to All
  American Asphalt for the 2020 Pavement Rehabilitation Project, Contract No.
  20-12;
  2. Rejected the submitted bid protest filed by Manhole Adjusting Incorporated as
  without merit;
  3. Approved plans and specifications for the 2020 Pavement Rehabilitation
  Project, Contract No. 20-12;
  4. Authorized the City Manager to execute contract documents with All American
  Asphalt for the total bid amount in the amount of $1,195,276; and

CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  October 27, 2020
   5. Approved a Purchase Order in the amount of $1,314,804 which includes a 10%
  construction contingency.

4. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES OPTIONS

  The staff presentation was made by Assistant City Manager/Community
  Development Director Chaparyan and Economic Development Manager Domenica
  Megerdichian.

  City Manager Lazzaretto clarified that the consultant who is working on an analysis
  of a joint powers authority option should have the report completed in March or
  April of 2021, and it will be presented to the City Council for consideration as a
  separate item.

  The following provided comments in support of the City continuing its association
  with the San Gabriel Valley Human Society (SGVHS): Nancy Chlaifour; Karen Smith,
  San Marino resident; Kathleen Hernandez and family, residents; Melissa Arellano;
  Vanessa Zamalloa, Temple City resident; Heather Mnoian; Michael Green; Angel
  Covarrubias, Alhambra resident; Sue Fitzsimmons; Charmaine Liccardi; Jenny
  Zamalloa-Ward; Nancy Kong; Virginia Gladwin; Isela Bowles, resident and business
  owner; and Karen McCarley.

  George Valdez provided comments in favor of a hybrid approach to animal services
  where the City handles some services in-house and sub-contracts out those it can’t.

  Cheryl Cabot, resident, provided comments in favor of finding an alternative
  company to handle animal services.

  Discussion included the City receiving a credit for dog license fees received for the
  fiscal year if the agreement is renewed for another six months; an audit or review
  of SGVHS records and what information that would provide; changes in SGVHS
  operations due to COVID-19; shelter capacity and planned improvements; cat-
  licensing; disease-control and spay/neuter programs and services; adoption
  services; possibility of the City doing licensing and animal-related code
  enforcement in-house; comparison of a hybrid service model versus contracting
  with SGVHS for all services; site utilization; the SGVHS is a 501(c)(3) organization
  which may self-determine its purpose and policies; and the importance of having
  good animal services for the community.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to request an audit of SGVHS records
  and to direct staff to bring back a six-month agreement extension with SGVHS at
  $175,000 for City Council consideration.

5. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca adjourned the meeting at 8:42 P.M.
